original_prompt: A continuous 20-second first-person walking tour of the warm house in the starting image, with lively, deliberate looking around. Walk forward immediately, turn left through the living-room arch and pass around the end of the cream sofa. A ginger tabby is chilling on the inner sofa cushion, breathing gently with an occasional small ear or tail-tip movement. A small physical model locomotive with two short carriages continuously travels clockwise around a fixed oval track on the floor in front of the fireplace. They are initially hidden by the sofa back and arch, and are naturally revealed as we enter; give both a clear view in the first eight seconds. Keep walking around the sofa and look right at the fireplace and painting. From eight to twelve seconds, walk forward, look up to the timber beam and back down. From twelve to sixteen seconds, move toward the tall windows and look across them, then return the gaze to the interior. From sixteen to twenty seconds, step backward to widen the same room and see the same lounging cat and still-circling train again. Keep the sofa, fireplace, windows and fixed track in the same places throughout, even while out of view. One unbroken shot at natural speed, with real walking parallax. Keep the early cat-and-train reveal at normal adult eye height, with the train readable below the fireplace in the same room view.
